title: Facet primes and normalized monomial valuations of complete toric models
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q
eq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(	heta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $	heta-p\in(z^q\ (q
eq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Write $z^q$ for the chart monomials in $R$. Assume $R$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Put $G=P^{m gp}$, let $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, and let $\sigma\subset V$ be the cone of nonnegative rational linear combinations of the images of $P$. A facet is a face of $\sigma$ of codimension one; explicitly it is a subset $F=\sigma\cap\ker h$, for a nonzero rational linear form $h:V	o\mathbf Q$ nonnegative on $\sigma$, with $\dim F=\dim V-1$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the set of facets. Then $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and every $z^q$ is nonzero. The set $\mathcal F$ is finite, and for each $F\in\mathcal F$ there is a unique homomorphism $
u_F:G	o\mathbf Z$ nonnegative on $P$, with image $\mathbf Z$ and $F=\sigma\cap\ker
u_F$. These forms satisfy
$$\sigma=\{v\in V:
u_F(v)\geq0	ext{ for all }F\in\mathcal F\},$$
where each $
u_F$ is extended rationally to $V$. The ideals
$$\mathfrak p_F=(z^q:q\in P,\ q
otin F)R$$
are distinct height-one prime ideals, and they are exactly the height-one prime ideals of $R$ containing at least one chart monomial $z^q$. Height one means that the prime is nonzero and no prime lies strictly between it and $(0)$. The local ring $R_{\mathfrak p_F}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Its normalized additive valuation $v_F:\operatorname{Frac}(R)^	imes	o\mathbf Z$ (a uniformizer has value one) satisfies
$$v_F(z^q)=
u_F(q)\qquad(q\in P).$$
For $P=\{0\}$ the facet set and the list of boundary primes are empty, and the displayed half-space intersection is $V=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-sharp-cone-primitive-facet-preparation] to the given sharp fs monoid. Obtain the finite free lattice $G$, $P=\sigma\cap G$, the finite facet set, its unique primitive normals, the half-space equality and the witnesses $f_F\in P\cap F$ positive on all other facets.

source.place: Agent-written short assembly of the four re-split arguments for the models of Expose VI 1.6, printed p. 70; retained old steps 1--18.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-sharp-monoid-positive-grading] on the lattice and sharp monoid from Step 1 to choose $w$ positive off zero. Set $T=P\times\mathbf N^n\subset G\times\mathbf Z^n$, a finitely generated submonoid of a finite free group, and $W(q,e)=w(q)+\sum e_i$; this is positive off zero. A field is Noetherian and complete for $(0)$; a Cohen ring is a complete local PID by [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], hence Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-complete-model-coefficient-nonvanishing] to $A=L,T,W$. Relabelling $z^{(q,e)}=z^qt^e$ identifies the rings and completion ideals: a nonzero $(q,e)$ has $q\ne0$ or some $e_i>0$, so its monomial is divisible by a displayed chart generator; conversely those generators are product monomials. In the Cohen case $\theta$ has constant coefficient $p$, since every chart generator has positive weight and convolution gives zero constant coefficient for each of its multiples, hence for their finite sums. Here $p$ is nonzero and a nonunit. Thus $R$ is Noetherian and every chart monomial survives in both cases.

proof.text:
For a facet $F$, put $S=P\cap F$. Nonnegativity of $
u_F$ shows that $a+b\in S$ forces $a,b\in S$, so $S$ is a face. Apply [lem-trf-complete-model-face-quotients]. Its kernel generators, and their images in the Cohen quotient, identify its ideal with the displayed $\mathfrak p_F$. Its quotient isomorphism makes $\mathfrak p_F$ prime, and its membership criterion says $z^q\in\mathfrak p_F$ exactly when $q
otin F$, equivalently $
u_F(q)>0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monomial-boundary-localizations] with $I=\mathcal F$, the normals and witnesses of Step 1, and the ring and chart of Steps 2--3. Its half-space hypothesis on $P$ is the combination of $P=\sigma\cap G$ and the cone half-space equality. The group completion is generated by $P$, and sharpness gives $P\cap(-P)=\{0\}$. Each $\nu_F$ is surjective by Step 1. The assumed domain $R$ is Noetherian by Step 2, and its chart obeys $z^0=1$ and $z^{q+q'}=z^qz^{q'}$ by construction. Step 3 supplies primality and exact monomial membership. Thus every hypothesis of the localization lemma holds. It gives distinct nonzero height-one boundary primes, exhaustion of the height-one primes containing monomials, and DVR localizations with $v_F(z^q)=\nu_F(q)$.

proof.text: For $P=\{0\}$, Step 1 gives $G=V=0$ and no facets. The only chart monomial is $1$, in no prime, and the empty half-space intersection is $V=0$. Step 2 still applies. All arguments permit $n=0$, when $T=P$. These observations give every degenerate clause.
